newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian parliament votes pay freeze for deputies.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian parliament votes pay freeze for deputies.

text.p: Parliament in crisis-ridden Bulgaria voted on Friday to freeze deputies' wages at September levels until year's end as an austerity measure, state radio reported.
Monthly inflation is running at more than 18 percent and the national currency has collapsed from 70 levs to the dollar in January to 216 now.

The head of the opposition Union of Democratic Forces parliamentary bloc, Yordan Sokolov, dismissed the measure as a pre-election publicity stunt by the ruling Socialists who, with their leftist coalition allies, hold 125 seats in the 240-seat parliament.
A presidential election is scheduled on October 27.
The measure was passed after a stormy debate in which deputies traded accusations about who had expensive cars and who should be responsible for paying parliamentarians' mobile phone bills.
Deputies' wages are calculated from the national average monthly wage for the past three months. The average pre-tax salary for a deputy is 48,000 levs ($222.3) a month.

The measure applies to cabinet ministers and state employees up to head of department level but Ventsislav Dimitrov of the small People's Union party said the move was scarcely worthwhile as it would save not more than four million levs. ($1=215.90 Leva)
